False news quickly spreads on social media, often rising to trending topics in a matter of hours, yet by the time it reaches regular users, the information's accuracy is uncertain. This framework utilises an initialization phase where the promising combination of sources and categories is identified through a small dataset from a trusted dataset. A dataset with nine classes was utilized, although one class was removed due to its small size. We employed a multi-classifier ensemble consisting of 13 convolutional neural networks (CNN), combining their outputs to classify lesions. To handle outliers, an outlier detection method using PHP and RCD (Rejection Curve based on Mahalanobis distance) was developed and integrated into the challenge. A single CNN was used to predict entropy values, which helped in removing outliers. Ultimately, a single-band RGB image was preferred over polorized and multispectral images for analysis. A dataset with 1000 images was used to train the machines, with an additional 100 images used to calculate entropy. The results showed that a single-band RGB image yielded the best outcomes, with a precision of 0.814 and an AUC score of 0.992 on average. The most frequent diagnoses in the dataset were melanoma, acral melanoma, basal cell carcinoma, squamous cell carcinoma, actinic keratoses, benign nevi, seborrheic keratoses, angiomas, and inflammatory lesions. The outcomes also demonstrated that removing outliers significantly improved the analysis accuracy. The best precision achieved was 0.933 and the best AUC score was 0.994.
